title: Boss: the untestable reminder service
summary: Rescue a reminder service that reads the clock, the console and a random generator directly.

steps.title: The untestable
steps.body: `ReminderService` decides which reminders are due, picks a random cheerful sign-off, and prints to the console, all in one method, with `DateTime.Now` and `new Random()` inside. You will make it testable in three moves: a pure core, injected dependencies, and tests of your own.

steps.title: Pure core
prompt: Write the pure decision as a static method:
- `static class Reminders` with `static List<string> Due(IEnumerable<Reminder> all, DateTime now)` returning the texts of reminders whose `DueAt` is at or before `now`, earliest first
solution: public static List<string> Due(IEnumerable<Reminder> all, DateTime now) =>
template: Dojo.Eq("due ones, earliest first", new List<string> { "standup", "lunch" }, Reminders.Due(dojoAll, dojoNow));
Dojo.Eq("none due", new List<string>(), Reminders.Due(dojoAll, dojoNow.AddDays(-1)));

steps.title: Inject the shell's dependencies
prompt: `Reminder` and `Reminders.Due` are given. Rewrite `ReminderService` so every hidden input comes through its constructor:
- `ReminderService(Func<DateTime> now, Func<int, int> pick, TextWriter output)`
- `void Run(IEnumerable<Reminder> all)` writes each due text on its own line, then one sign-off: `SignOffs[pick(SignOffs.Length)]`
starter: public static List<string> Due(IEnumerable<Reminder> all, DateTime now) =>
static readonly string[] SignOffs = { "You got this!", "Go team!", "Onward!" };
foreach (var text in Reminders.Due(all, DateTime.Now)) Console.WriteLine(text);
solution: public static List<string> Due(IEnumerable<Reminder> all, DateTime now) =>
class ReminderService(Func<DateTime> now, Func<int, int> pick, TextWriter output)
static readonly string[] SignOffs = { "You got this!", "Go team!", "Onward!" };
foreach (var text in Reminders.Due(all, now())) output.WriteLine(text);
template: new ReminderService(() => dojoT, n => n - 1, dojoW).Run(new[] { new Reminder("tea", dojoT.AddMinutes(-1)), new Reminder("later", dojoT.AddHours(1)) });
new ReminderService(() => dojoT.AddHours(2), _ => 0, dojoW2).Run(new[] { new Reminder("tea", dojoT.AddMinutes(-1)), new Reminder("later", dojoT.AddHours(1)) });
Dojo.Eq("later, with another sign-off", "tea|later|You got this!", dojoW2.ToString().Trim().Replace("\r\n", "|").Replace("\n", "|"));

steps.title: Your own tests for the core
prompt: Write `List<string> TestDue(Func<IEnumerable<Reminder>, DateTime, List<string>> due)` that passes for the correct `Reminders.Due` and catches the broken versions the checker tries:
- using `<` instead of `<=` (a reminder due exactly now is missed)
- returning reminders that are **not** yet due
starter: void Expect(string name, bool ok) { if (!ok) failed.Add(name); }
solution: void Expect(string name, bool ok) { if (!ok) failed.Add(name); }
Expect("due exactly now is included", result.Contains("now"));
template: List<string> DojoGood(IEnumerable<Reminder> all, DateTime now) => all.Where(r => r.DueAt <= now).OrderBy(r => r.DueAt).Select(r => r.Text).ToList();
Dojo.Eq("the correct version passes all your checks", new List<string>(), TestDue(DojoGood));
Dojo.Check("catches: < instead of <=", TestDue((a, n) => a.Where(r => r.DueAt < n).OrderBy(r => r.DueAt).Select(r => r.Text).ToList()).Count > 0, "missing the reminder due now passed");
Dojo.Check("catches: not sorted", TestDue((a, n) => a.Where(r => r.DueAt <= n).Select(r => r.Text).ToList()).Count > 0, "an unsorted version passed");
Dojo.Check("catches: future included", TestDue((a, n) => a.OrderBy(r => r.DueAt).Select(r => r.Text).ToList()).Count > 0, "a version returning everything passed");
hints: Put reminders in the input out of order, one due exactly `now`, and one in the future.
Compare `string.Join(",", result)` with the exact expected order.
